REPORT AT A GLANCE 
 
 
 
Roads 
Offaly County Council received the 2020 
National Roads Allocation of €3,169,755 
from the TII, the 2020 Regional and Local 
Roads Allocation of €11,027,499 from the 
Department of Transport, Tourism and 
Sport. In summary the 2020 initial Roads 
Budget is €16,064,384 representing a 
10% increase on the 2019 budget.  
 
 
 
Local 
Community 
Development 
Committee (LCDC) 
The LCDC met on 16th January 2020.  
The 2019 Annual Report of the Local 
Community Development Committee was 
adopted by the members. 
 
 
 
New eServices in Offaly Libraries 
During February 2020, two new service 
providers for online resources will 
contribute to our eServices offer in Offaly 
Libraries.  Transparent Languages online 
will replace Mango Languages and 
provide online language learning and 
Pressreader will become the library online 
newspaper provider, replacing Proquest.   
 
D A T E S  F O R  Y O U R  D I A R Y  
 
BREXIT CUSTOMS WORKSHOP – 24TH FEBRUARY 2020 
The Customs Export & Import Procedures workshop will 
take place in the Tullamore Court Hotel on Monday, 24th 
February 2020. 
 
LEAP INTO LIBRARIES: #LEAPINTOLIBRARIES  
A national Leap into Libraries day planned for the 29th 
February.  All 8 libraries in Offaly will host a programme 
of events ranging from Arts and Crafts and Origami 
workshops to Creative Music and Play sessions.  
https://www.offaly.ie/eng/Services/Libraries/Events/   
 
LOCAL ENTERPRISE WEEK 2ND – 6TH MARCH 
Events will be held in a number of locations – Tullamore, 
Edenderry, Birr and Ferbane. To attend events please visit 
www.localenterprise.ie/offaly to reserve a place.  
 
FREE BUSINESS ADVICE SESSIONS ON ECOMMERCE GRANTS 
A free 45-minute one-to-one mentoring session on how to 
set up an ecommerce website and avail of grants will be held 
on Wednesday 4th March 2020.

ROADS 
Offaly County Council received the 2020 
National Roads Allocation of €3,169,755 
from the TII. The allocation includes funding 
for the N52 Tullamore to Kilbeggan Link 
major scheme, N62 Cloghan to Derrinlough 
peat replacement minor works scheme. 
€1.5m has been allocated for pavement 
schemes and €500,000 for Road Safety 
Improvement Schemes.   
 
Offaly County Council received the 2020 
Regional and Local Roads Allocation of 
€11,027,499 from the Department of 
Transport, Tourism and Sport in January. 
This included two specific improvement 
grants for the Edenderry Inner Relief Road 
and the Birr Distributor Road.  
 
Offaly County Council has 
allocated 
€1,867,130 from own resources. In summary 
therefore, the 2020 initial Roads Budget is 
€16,064,384 representing a 10% increase on 
the 2019 budget.

ENVIRONMENT & WATER 
Environment 
A total of 98 complaints in relation to waste 
and litter were made to date in 2020.  No 
legal action has been instigated this year so 
far.  
 
Burial Grounds 
Part 8 approval was obtained for Kilreahan 
Cemetery at the September 2019 Council 
meeting and the next step is to prepare the 
tender documents Part 8 Public Consultation 
for Kilcoursey Cemetery in Clara open until 
25th February.  
 
Water Services - Capital Projects 
Works are progressing at Tullamore, Birr 
and Clonaslee. Rehabilitation works at 
Clonin will proceed in 2020 while Croghan 
& Newtown are at design stage. IW are 
currently 
preparing 
the 
design 
for 
replacement reservoir at Clonbullogue and 
considering a replacement reservoir at Walsh 
Island. 
 
LOCAL & COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT 
Local 
Community 
Development 
Committee (LCDC) 
The LCDC met on 16th January 2020.  The 
2019 
Annual 
Report 
of 
the 
Local 
Community Development Committee was 
adopted by the members. Agenda items 
included Rural Development LEADER 
Programme 2014 – 2020 and an update on 
the Healthy Offaly Work Plan.  Members 
approved the Healthy Offaly Programme for 
2019-2021. 
 
Age Friendly Strategy 
The Age Friendly Co-ordinator attended the 
first meeting of the Offaly Older Persons’ 
Network 2020 where plans for 2020 actions 
were discussed. 
 
Public Participation Network 
The PPN Resource Workers held their 
meeting in Trinity Place Dublin on Jan 15th 
The PPN Secretariat held their first meeting 
of 2020 on the evening of 15th Jan with a 
discussion on the work plan for 2020 and 
upcoming elections for some of the PPN 
reps.  
The Resource Worker represented the PPN at 
the CCTV meetings. The Resource Worker 
made a presentation to the Housing & 
Disability steering group on the disability 
linkage group ODEN.  
The Garda Community Day took place in 
Mucklagh on Jan 31st. The PPN also 
participated in the Community Awards 
meeting.      
 
Comhairle na nÓg 
The first Comhairle na nÓg meeting of 2020 
took place on 22nd January 2020 where new 
members were welcomed to the group and 
given an overview of project work to date.  
Members met with film producer Mr. Garrett 
Daly to discuss to the shooting of their 
upcoming YouTube video in relation to 
exam stress. 
 
Community CCTV 
A Project Team meeting was held with 3 
proposed Community CCTV schemes in 
Tullamore on 22nd January 2020 to progress 
their applications with further meetings 
scheduled for March.

LIBRARY SERVICES 
National Campaign promoting Libraries: 
#Takeacloserlook  
 
 
This national advertising campaign is asking 
everyone to ‘Take a Closer Look’ at what 
their local authority library has to offer and 
was launched on the 20th January 2020.  
Offaly 
Library 
Service 
has 
proudly 
embraced the campaign, which is running 
across radio, cinema, TV on demand, digital 
and social media. The aim of the campaign is 
to encourage people of all ages to join and 
use the library. The ‘Take a Closer Look’ 
campaign was devised by the Libraries 
Development Unit of the LGMA with the 
support of the Department of Rural and 
Community Development. It is part a wider 
national 
strategy 
to 
increase 
library 
membership and usage in Ireland. See the 
‘Take 
a

advert 
at

Healthy Ireland at Your Library 
  
Offaly Libraries’ Healthy Ireland at Your 
Library programme is now entering its third 
year.  A 5-month  programme of 36 events 
for all ages groups is now finalised. The 
programme features a selection of public 
lectures in support of health and wellbeing by 
qualified practicioners and advocates. Events 
include “Let’s Get Messy: Exploring the 
benefits of Messy Play for children with 
ASD” and “Navigating the Wobbly World 
of Anxienty: helping parents to cope with 
the challenges of childhood”, as well as 
talks on dealing with Arthritis, Dementia 
Impacts, Exam Stress and much more. Full 
details can be found at  www.offaly.ie/libraries  
An updated reading collection has also been 
added to our Healthy Ireland collection for 
2020, embedding Offaly libraries as a 
valuable source of health information in the 
local community. 
 
Harry Potter Book Night: Tullamore Library 
 
Harry Potter Book Night is an annual Offaly 
Library Service programme and is in its third 
year. This ever popular event promotes 
children’s 
literacy 
and 
reading 
development and 
is a key pillar of 
Offaly’s Right to Read Campaign. On the 
Thursday 6th February (4.00pm – 8.00pm), 
Tullamore library became home to all things 
Harry Potter with our own Offaly Tri-
wizard Tournament involving dragon eggs, 
spells and some Vex Robots! The evening 
was a huge success with over 300 wizards 
and their ‘muggle’ parents in attendance who 
enjoyed Quidditch Pong, Face Painting, our 
Costume Competition and a wonderful 
family-friendly Magic Show which closed 
the evening’s Harry Potter celebrations.   
 
Vex IQ Robotics at Offaly Libraries  
  The 
Offaly 
Primary 
School 
County Final for 
the 
Vex 
IQ 
challenge 
was 
held on Friday 31st January in Colaiste 
Choilm with 28 schools taking part.  It was a 
great event with positive comments received 
from teachers, pupils, parents and volunteers.  
The library service is an enthusiastic partner 
on Vex projects providing support, access to 
robots and programming software in the 
library environment.  This programme 
ensures today’s students are qualified for the 
jobs of tomorrow. It’s an ideal introduction 
for students who we hope will drive Offaly’s 
economic ambitions, support innovation and 
provide foundations for future prosperity in 
the county.   
The Offaly Secondary School County final 
for the Vex robotics competition – “Tower 
Takeover” will take place on Monday 10th 
February in Sacred Heart School with 5 
schools competing to become the Offaly 
Excellence Champion.  The library service 
will again provide volunteers to support this 
final.   
 
Clara Library Opening Hours 
Offaly Library Service is delighted to 
announce that Clara Library has returned to 
full opening hours with library access now 
available on Wednesday evenings and 
Saturday mornings.  The Clara library team 
are busily engaged in developing the library 
collections and a programme of outreach and 
library events for the benefit of all the 
community.   
 
New eServices in Offaly Libraries 
During February 2020, two new service 
providers for online resources will contribute 
to our eServices offer in Offaly Libraries.

Transparent Languages online will replace 
Mango Languages and provide online 
language learning and Pressreader will 
become the library online newspaper 
provider, replacing Proquest.   
Transparent Languages is a complete 
language-learning system for independent 
learners with 100+ languages, flexible 
learning paths, extensive English collection, 
core skill building exercises and course 
completion certificate.   
Press reader has access to over 7,000 
newspapers from around the world, available 
to download immediately to 5 different 
devises and instantly translates articles into 
16 languages. 
Both resources are free of charge to all 
library members.  
  
The Acorn Project Photographic Exhibition, 
“Our Town, Our Vision”, Edenderry Library 
 
This striking photographic exhibition opened 
in Edenderry Library on Wednesday 5th 
February and had a wonderful attendance at 
the launch. The exhibition will be on display 
until Friday 28th February 2020 (during 
library opening hours) and the Acorn Project 
invite you to join them on a journey through 
our community, via photography! 
  
Lastly, don’t forget all upcoming library 
events for the month ahead can be found at 
https://www.offaly.ie/eng/Services/Libraries
/Events/ 
 
LOCAL ENTERPRISE OFFICE 
Showcase 2020 
The Local Enterprise Office Offaly attended 
Showcase 2020 in the RDS Arena, Dublin. 
Heartworks from Tullamore exhibited at the 
event. Showcase 2020 is Ireland’s Creative 
Expo for Irish designer and craft business. 
Over 450 exhibitors including leading Irish 
designers and manufacturers and the very 
best emerging home grown creative talent 
attended the event. 
 
 
Upcoming Events and New Initiatives 
GradStart scheme now available for LEO 
clients 
The GradStart scheme is a 24-month 
graduate placement programme with funding 
of up to €30k (€15k per year). Local 
Enterprise Office client companies with at 
least 5 full time staff can apply for the 
GradStart programme. 
 
The objective of GradStart is to assist 
indigenous companies to scale and grow 
their businesses through the introduction of 
good graduate talent (with a minimum Level 
6-degree qualification) to deliver clearly 
defined projects.

Digital Marketing for Business - This

Innovation Vouchers - open call 
Open call for applications continues for 
2020. Standard €5k vouchers are available to 
assist a company explore a business

knowledge provider. 
 
Spring Business Training Courses 
The Local Enterprise Office Offaly has 
launched the Spring Business Training 
Course schedule. Booking is now available 
for a number of courses such as Start your 
Own Business Course, Digital marketing for 
Business, Part-Time Business Start Up 
(while holding down a day job) and How to 
Sell Successfully.

Free Business Advice Sessions on eCommerce 
Grants 
A free 45-minute one-to-one mentoring 
session on how to set up an ecommerce 
website and avail of grants will be held on 
Wednesday 4th March 2020. The one to one 
mentoring session designed to help you get 
an application ready for the Trading Online 
Voucher Scheme. After this session you will 
have a clearer picture of what’s involved in 
running 
an 
eCommerce 
website, 
the 
practicalities, logistics and potential issues 
that may arise. 
 
Brexit Customs Workshop - Monday, 24 
February 2020 
The Customs Export & Import Procedures 
workshop will take place in the Tullamore 
Court Hotel on Monday, 24th February 2020. 
It covers how export and import customs 
procedures on trade with ‘Third Countries’ 
apply, how tariffs work and the need to 
correctly classify your goods.  
Attendance is free but early booking is 
essential. These workshops are fully funded 
by DBEI, through Enterprise Ireland and are 
delivered by Export-Edge Training, on 
behalf of Local Enterprise Office Offaly. 
 
Anna Marie Delaney, Chief Executive
